guards.what: G1 (DORMANT, and the port's stated premise is FALSE): 'the sim has no enchantments, so this is a no-op stub' (punch_dagger.py:8-9)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PunchDagger.cs:24-33 builds a CardSelectorPrefs for one card, resolves the canonical Momentum enchantment, awaits CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForEnchantment(Owner, Momentum, 5, prefs) and then CardCmd.Enchant(Momentum.ToMutable(), card, 5) on each returned card. THE PREMISE IS FALSE, confirmed by execution (`py tools/audit/relic_probes_b13.py stub-premises`): sts2_rl/enchantments.py ports 17 enchantments ['clone','corrupted','glam','goopy','imbued','instinct','nimble','perfect_fit','sharp','slither','souls','sown','spiral','steady','swift','tezcataras_ember','vigorous'], and a SIBLING RELIC already performs this exact pickup shape -- relics/beautiful_bracelet.py:23-29 filters the deck by `Enchantment.can_enchant`, calls run.select_cards('enchant', ...) and attaches the enchantment with an amount. So the machinery, the selector and the precedent all exist (PROMPT.md bug class 12: check the claim the stub rests on). Sweep C independently reached the same conclusion for this unit ('AfterObtained dispatched; no enchantments is FALSE'), and this record confirms rather than re-derives it. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING (rule 6, DORMANT with the unported thing NAMED): the Momentum ENCHANTMENT MODEL itself -- `'momentum' in ALL_ENCHANTMENTS` is False. Porting Momentum makes this live immediately, and the fix is then a five-line after_obtained copied from beautiful_bracelet. Filed as a gap and not a waiver because 'the sim has no such content yet' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). EXECUTED baseline for the fix: `run.add_relic('punch_dagger')` leaves every deck card's enchantment unchanged.

guards.what: N1: CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForEnchantment is a PLAYER CHOICE, and it draws no RNG
guards.rationale: Recorded as the contrast with this batch's relic/royal_stamp, whose AfterObtained UnstableShuffles the candidate list on `Rng.Niche` before offering it (RoyalStamp.cs:36) and therefore has an RNG-parity half this relic does not. Punch Dagger passes the deck straight to the selector with no shuffle and no stream named, so PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half (a named RNG stream silently falling back to the shared random) does not apply here -- checked whether the stream is CONSUMED, not merely named, as the class instructs. The sim's own selector (run.select_cards) is the counterpart for the choice itself. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs is not hashed by this record; the claim rests on PunchDagger.cs:26-32 having no shuffle call.
